**Note to the reader**: This is a living record of the Elder Dragons, their deaths, and how their fall has impacted the Tyrian ecosystem. Per standards and regulations, this is only intended to observe the effects of their falling while remaining factual about the cause.  
  
*Signed, A. Gray III, Lead Drakologist*  
  
_Foreword_   
  
The overall effects of the dragons and their deaths has been as unexpected and perplexing as it is concerning. Until recently, we had suspected that the dragons were plagued by some sort of corruption, such as the Dragonvoid, but it wasn't apparent until the death of Kralkatorrik and the eventual death of the Elder Mother. Soo-Won and Isgarren remained respectfully distant from one another, as Soo-Won sought to protect Tyria proper while Isgarren looked to the sky and the Mists beyond.  
  
The most notable change in the ecosystem was the swelling of the ley lines in the Maguuma Jungle. This may have been due to the temporary imbalance caused by Zhaitan's fall, but these surges were instrumental in the rise of the Jungle Dragon (also listed as the "Beast of the Coppice" in certain archives). The brewing ecological disaster was made all the worse when Scarlet Briar redirected some of these already unstable ley lines straight to Mordremoth's refuge. Some of these lines cross into the boundaries of the Horn, even, where Amnytas has been settled since Mother's Fall. These lines have behaved as expected, although some fluctuations were noted in the spire before its fracturing (triggered by the blast of magical energies immediately following Soo-Won's death; stability was gained again once Aurene, the Prismatic Dragon, took over as the filter moments later). The result of the spire's fracturing was catastrophic, however, allowing Kryptis and other sentience from farther realms to intrude. This research is ongoing.     
  
Escalations would continue with Mordremoth's death, then Kralkatorrik's. Research is still being done on the overall effects of Primordus and Jormag's more...recent blight, but strange activities were noted all along the greater Shiverpeaks. Pockets of thicker magic have begun swelling in most regions, causing more magically attuned births and other ecological effects. Some witnesses have reported enhanced agricultural effects (lands impacted by Zhaitan being a pleasant surprise), while others, especially in areas impacted by Kralkatorrik and Jormag, have reported a steep decline in feasible land use.  
  
All research is now pivoting to the rise of Aurene and her living champion(s). The Prismatic Dragon is now sleeping, and despite rising tensions with threats from the Mists, the overall ecosystem seems to be calming once again.
Capture and commune with the altar in the Edge of the Mists.

The Voice of Fate calls upon me  
to see the journey of the Unseen  
to eternal fruition.  
So with tomorrow's sun  
dawns a new era.  
Anointed by its rays,  
we venture forth, three pilgrims  
whose destinies entwine to weave  
a transcendent tapestry  
of the divine.

Ulrich returned. His lone communions with the wild rarely last long. He spoke little. And so we went on preparing a meager supper as if nothing had come to pass. We ate mostly in silence. That is, until the fire began to dwindle...

Out of the dark, the voice called unto them. For it was they who had been chosen to realize the mission of the Unseen Ones.

And thus, it spoke to them, "Chosen three... You are destined... Seek the gate..."

"As the sun dawns across the wilds... You shall hear my voice... And I will be your guide... You who must open the gate... So fate has written it... So make it be..."
 
To think mere hours ago, our vision was clouded by woes ephemeral. We are so close. Though I can't recall my last full meal, my mind has never felt so sated.
Awarded for completing the story step "Enemy of My Enemy."

After Westergard found that old journal, everyone's been wanted to carve out some sort of town history for Hullgarden. Aside from stories told by the folks that have been here longest—current winner being Granny Bog, sitting pretty at ninety-six years—we don't know a whole lot.   
   
Granny Bog says that when her grandpap's grandpap arrived at Castora, all they could find was a couple of hulls dragged up shore. Found an old firepit, too, but it hadn't been used in months—or years. They turned those hulls into Hullgarden and the rest is history. But who knows how many "Hullgardens" there were before us... I shudder to think how many souls have been stranded here. Probably fared a whole lot worse than us, too.  
  
At least the excitement is keeping everyone busy. Not a lot of surprises these days.

Komalie very well may fall, and if it does, so will Bava Nisos. They will come for us.  
  
Half of our ranks are ill or enraged by the poison's curse now, even those we thought tolerant. Every day since Otho returned with the gate, its otherworldly energies have penetrated every corner and every mind. The dead nearly outnumber the living.  
  
All of our children, the gildless—they're all gone. All of them. Gone.  
  
And then there's Manikaz. He, in absolute desperation, has turned into a being of pure bloodlust. He is now done with the city of Gavril—the White Mantle surrendered all of them to us. And now he turns to them, our devout. All blood for the stone, even though that effort feels far from useful. The gate does not want to be opened, and the keystone is plump from the feast.
She is too full to eat any more today.

I am nervous.

Mentor Sidony assures me that the rite of Divitium Nava is as much about the ceremony as the trials. As one who has always done their due diligence, I sought out the accounts of other candidates; at least those who took the time to write down their experiences.

To my surprise, I could find only four accounts that detailed the trials themselves with any veracity. Mentor Sidony informed me that the reason for this is simple: the trial chamber is never the same. It is designed to construct itself around the candidate, ensuring that no two candidates ever experience the trials within the same way.

Based on the accounts I read—which Mentor Sidony confirmed—the trials are always divided into three sections: trials of the body, trials of the mind, and trials of the spirit.

This information has not comforted me nor quelled my anxiety, however. If anything, it has made my stomach twist itself into knots. I feel ill...

strings.en:
This dry and litigious text is filled mostly with banal verdicts issued by the Ministry of Justice in disputed legal cases. However, there is one exception: A case between the Ministry of Purity and the imperial regent once Emperor Bitgaram had become too ill to govern. As the emperor's daughter was still a child at the time, the minister argued that the powers invested in his office to combat the Risen (in particular, that he "speaks with the emperor's voice") gave him the authority to overrule the candidate brought by the Imperial Court. The text records a heated dispute, decided along razor-thin margins in favor of the minister.

Members of the review panel arguing against the minister's position reappear later in the book, charged with "sedition and impure practices."
